claims.statement: The fixed clean runtime bundle passes stopped upgrade, suffix-preserving rollback, complete cold backup and relocated restore, actual O1 capacity/fault/restart observations, every frozen probe and fresh inherited M14 qualification.

limitations: Finite evidence: 22 case families, 109 variants, 118 mandatory probes and applicable conditional controls are not exhaustive exploration or formal proof.
Two three-member groups, a durable sink and two publishers run on one host. Process fail-stop does not prove host, rack, region, arbitrary-partition or power-loss isolation.

The supported version switch stops every runtime role before replacing the complete original classpath. Rolling or mixed-version operation, online migration and changed application/wire formats are not qualified.

Cold backup captures the named nonempty cut A. Suffix-preserving rollback instead reopens CURRENT N data. A backup from an older cut is not an equivalent rollback of later trades. Bundle/backup inventories retain the frozen portable path grammar; other trees with unsupported native diagnostic filenames fail closed instead of renaming or omitting files.

Relocated restore uses a new absolute root on the same host with the same ports and identities. Cross-host restore, port migration, encryption, access-control infrastructure and off-host backup custody are outside this run.

The separately frozen mark-termination amendment corrects the original stop contract. A -1 sentinel alone is insufficient: positive live anchors, real normal-close and PID/startInstant exit evidence, two complete header reads and strict age/inventory bounds remain required.

O1 contains 6250 planned logical arrivals, including 250 warmup and 250 fault arrivals. Queue refusals, transport not-submitted, original UNKNOWN outcomes, same-identity retries, controls and preludes remain separate. These observations are not a universal TPS, latency, RTO, RPO or SLO guarantee.

Timing uses actual controller observations on one monotonic clock. Reading a durable receipt bounds observation time; it does not measure the sink's internal force completion instant. Market snapshot state coverage is not delivery of missing historical trades.

Full M14 histories and diagnostics remain enabled without pruning. Snapshot, restart, retained identity memory and diagnostic cost grow with history; no constant-memory or long-duration capacity claim is made. The inherited finite history guard can also refuse ACK controls.

External publication is at least once. Stable identity and durable sink frontiers support idempotent replay, but transport acknowledgements are not business settlement or distributed exactly-once effects. Trusted controller authorization is not production IAM or TLS.

Execution saturation refuses new work atomically; Market retention is lossy and a whole-shard snapshot cannot recover missing trade history. The finite Q1 window is not an archival service or an unbounded outage tolerance.

The two frozen synthetic C06 controls never count as runtime arrivals, attempts, trades or new UNKNOWN witnesses. Real IO, parser and component failures are preserved as infrastructure failures, never semantic-mutant kills.

Existing M13 import limits, message-size bounds, static append-only routing and per-shard history semantics remain unchanged. Counter, REST, balances, holds, settlement and new trading features are outside matching-1.0.1.

Fresh inherited M14 and M13 reports are exported losslessly as indexed original ZIP entries. They are diagnostic evidence, not replacement runtime backups; the complete original compressed backup is exported separately.

The failed matching-1.0.0 release CI runs retain their original tags and SYSTEM_ERROR classifications. A separately frozen publication correction fixes qualification timing only; selected original failure records are provenance inputs, not passing qualification results or a complete archive of those failed runs.
